aboutGame.title: What is Halo Flashpoint?
paragraphs: Halo Flashpoint is a two-player tabletop miniatures skirmish game from Mantic Games, set in the Halo universe. Instead of commanding sprawling armies, each player controls a small fireteam of three to six models, built from Spartans, ODSTs, Marines, Elites, Grunts, Brutes, and iconic heroes, on a compact battlefield that fits on a kitchen table.

Games run about 45 to 90 minutes and reward positioning over raw dice luck. Alternating activations keep both players involved in every round, energy shields soak up incoming fire before a model takes real damage, and dense terrain decides who can shoot and who has to move. Objective-driven scenarios mean a fireteam that holds ground usually beats one that only chases kills.

modules.name: Halo Flashpoint Beginner Guide
modules.description: Start with the core set, assemble a legal fireteam, and play a full Halo Flashpoint scenario without drowning in rules.

highlights.detail: Pick a starter or core set and check the contents before you build anything.
Assemble a legal fireteam: three to six models per side is standard skirmish size.
Lay out terrain with a mix of cover and open lanes so movement actually matters.
Learn the activation loop: alternate models, then move, shoot, fight, or interact.
Play an objective scenario and score points instead of chasing kills.
Review the roster after the game and swap one unit to see what changes.

faq.title: Halo Flashpoint FAQ
faq.description: Straight answers to the questions new players ask most about Halo Flashpoint, from how many models you need to how a game is actually won.

items.question: What is Halo Flashpoint?
items.answer: Halo Flashpoint is a two-player tabletop miniatures skirmish game from Mantic Games. Each player commands a small fireteam of Spartans, ODSTs, Marines, Elites, Grunts, or Brutes on a compact battlefield and fights over mission objectives rather than wiping out the opposing army.

items.question: How many miniatures do I need to play Halo Flashpoint?
items.answer: A standard Halo Flashpoint fireteam is roughly three to six models per side. That low model count keeps games fast, affordable, and easy to learn compared with mass-battle wargames.

items.question: How long does a game of Halo Flashpoint take?
items.answer: Most Halo Flashpoint games finish in about 45 to 90 minutes on a battlefield of roughly 2 by 2 to 3 by 3 feet, which makes it easy to fit a match into an evening.

items.question: Do I have to paint my Halo Flashpoint miniatures before playing?
items.answer: No. Bare plastic or primer is completely legal, and most new players get several Halo Flashpoint games in before they pick up a brush. Painting is a hobby layer on top of the rules, not a requirement.

items.question: How do you actually win a game of Halo Flashpoint?
items.answer: Halo Flashpoint is won on mission objectives. Scenarios define the scoring conditions, so a fireteam that holds ground and completes objectives usually beats one that only chases kills.
